explanation: Gift-giving is a warm, appreciated gesture in Brazil, both socially and in business, though business gifts should stay modest to avoid any appearance of bribery. A few specific things to avoid: wrapping a gift in purple (associated with mourning), giving anything sharp like knives (seen as symbolically 'cutting' the relationship), and giving a gift to someone of the opposite gender outside of a birthday, which can be misread as a romantic gesture rather than simple courtesy.
local_tip: Choose a modest, thoughtful gift, avoid purple wrapping paper and sharp objects, and be mindful that opposite-gender gifts outside of birthdays can send an unintended romantic signal.

also_check.note: Gift-giving is highly ritualized; avoid white flowers or sets of four, and present gifts with both hands.
Gifts are often unnecessary in business contexts; if given, keep them small and practical.
Gifts are welcomed, but avoid alcohol or pigskin products, and use the right hand to give and receive.

sources.title: Brazilian Culture - Etiquette, The Cultural Atlas
